extracted.intended_audience: YouTube creators, video producers, and digital marketers/SEO professionals aiming to improve video visibility
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and evaluative criteria for optimizing YouTube videos and channels (both long-form and Shorts) to rank higher in Search, Recommendations, and the Shorts feed in 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch Time & View Duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch time remains the most influential YouTube ranking factor in 2026 because it directly reflects how long users stay engaged on the platform. YouTube evaluates the total number of minutes viewers spend watching a video across all sessions, along with the average view duration per viewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer videos do not rank automatically; only content that maintains engagement throughout its duration signals high value. Optimize content to maximize total minutes watched and average view duration across sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience Retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience retention measures how much of a video viewers actually watch and plays a critical role in ranking performance. YouTube closely analyzes retention graphs to identify early exits, drop-off patterns, and overall viewing consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong retention—especially during the opening portion—indicates content meets expectations. Fix early drop-offs by improving hooks (first 15–30 seconds) and mid-video engagement techniques; poor retention suppresses distribution even with high initial clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Click-Through Rate (CTR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Click-through rate represents how often users choose a video after seeing it in search results or recommendations. CTR is influenced primarily by the effectiveness of a video’s thumbnail image, Video Titles, and title length in communicating relevance and value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CTR must be evaluated together with retention—high CTR with low retention signals misleading content and will lower rankings. In 2026 CTR is evaluated in real-time across a 7-day window after publish (changed from a 48-hour window). Aim for a sustained CTR above ~6% across broader audiences; new uploads from subscribers may see 10–15%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Metrics (likes, comments, shares, subscribers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement metrics help YouTube assess how viewers interact with a video beyond passive watching. Actions such as likes, comments, shares, and subscribers gained from a video provide confirmation that viewers find the content useful or interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early engagement after publishing is particularly valuable. Engagement strengthens ranking potential when combined with strong retention and watch time; encourage organic, meaningful interactions rather than incentivized low-effort actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword Optimization & Search Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Keyword optimization helps YouTube understand the topic and intent of a video so it can match the content to relevant search queries. Keywords placed naturally in Video Titles, descriptions, Video Tags, and spoken content improve discoverability without compromising trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on long-tail search terms and clear topic alignment rather than keyword stuffing. Spoken keywords via transcripts are increasingly weighted (spoken keyword density now influences search ranking). Use tools like Google Keyword Planner and Trends for research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Metadata Optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Video metadata provides structured information that supports accurate indexing and content classification. Clear titles, descriptive summaries, and relevant tags help YouTube associate videos with the correct search terms and audience segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload accurate closed captions and transcripts to improve semantic analysis and accessibility. Keep titles concise (<60 chars) with primary keywords; put primary/secondary keywords in the first 2–3 description lines; 300–500 word descriptions with long-tail phrases are recommended. Use 3–5 relevant tags (quality over quantity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Session Duration & Platform Retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Session duration measures how a video contributes to keeping viewers active on YouTube beyond a single view. Videos that encourage users to continue watching additional content signal strong platform value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: YouTube rewards videos that extend overall session length. Use end screens, internal suggestions, playlists, and sequencing to reduce exits and increase session continuation. Session contribution is prioritized by the recommendation engine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel Authority & Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel authority reflects the overall trust and performance history of a creator’s channel. YouTube considers factors such as upload frequency, topical focus, subscriber engagement, and accumulated watch history when evaluating new uploads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish consistently within a focused niche to build authority. Engagement rate per subscriber is more important than raw subscriber count; consistency helps establish trust signals but quality outweighs quantity (two high-quality videos/month > frequent low-quality uploads).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation System Signals (Home, Suggested, Shorts)
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube’s recommendation engine focuses on maximizing session duration and uses signals such as watch history, session duration, similar viewer behavior, and engagement signals to surface videos in Home, Suggested, and Shorts feeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create content that contributes to longer sessions and appeals to audiences with shared behavior. Strong performance in early tests increases reach; align thumbnails/titles to attract the right audience but prioritize satisfaction signals to maintain distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalized feeds ensure that viewers see content tailored to their unique behavior and interests. Results for the same query may differ between users based on watch history, interests, subscriptions, and engagement patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve personalization impact by aligning content to clear topic niches, using transcripts/automatic captions, and keeping topical consistency to match individual viewer preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Signals & Early Testing
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube continuously tests videos with real users to determine quality and relevance. Videos that perform well in early trials receive expanded reach, while poorly performing content may see limited distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize strong early metrics (retention, engagement velocity, CTR-with-retention) in the first minutes/hours to trigger wider tests. Promotion across social channels and embedding can help generate early traction for testing pools.

rubrics_metrics.name: User Satisfaction (qualitative satisfaction signals)
rubrics_metrics.description: User satisfaction is evaluated by retention, positive engagement, and reduced negative feedback. YouTube now emphasizes satisfaction to ensure algorithmic distribution aligns with genuine viewer value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and improve measurable satisfaction indicators (retention, likes, positive comments, low exit rates). Avoid misleading thumbnails/titles that increase clicks but lower satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorts: Swipe-Away Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Swipe-away rate is the percentage of viewers who swipe away within the first 1–2 seconds and functions as the Shorts equivalent of bounce rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize swipe-away by making the first frames compelling and clear. High swipe-away immediately suppresses distribution in the Shorts feed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorts: Loop Count
rubrics_metrics.description: Loop count measures how many times viewers replay your Short. Multiple loops signal extremely high satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design Shorts that reward replay (tight pacing, visual hooks, surprises) to increase loops; high loop counts are massively boosted in Shorts distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorts: Completion Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion rate is the percentage of viewers who watch your Short to the end. A completion rate above 80% is considered strong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep Shorts concise (15–45 seconds recommended) and optimize first frames; shorter Shorts (<30s) generally achieve higher completion rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorts: Engagement Velocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement velocity reflects how quickly likes, comments, and shares accumulate in the first 60 minutes after publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for rapid early engagement to trigger progressively larger audience tests; promote to existing audiences at publish to increase engagement velocity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorts: Audio & Trend Alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Using trending audio or original sounds can improve distribution by connecting Short content to active discovery trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage trending audio from Shorts libraries where appropriate and align content with active trends to improve discoverability; ensure audio choice matches content and adds value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorts: Caption Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding accurate captions to Shorts improves accessibility and helps the algorithm understand context. YouTube indexes captions for Shorts in 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate captions/transcripts for Shorts to enhance indexing and reach. Captions also aid comprehension and completion rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch Time Satisfaction Signals — Post-Watch Survey Responses
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube conducts real-time user surveys after video viewing — showing viewers simple satisfaction ratings. These survey results directly calibrate how the algorithm values a video’s watch time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Videos with high post-watch survey scores are amplified; aim to deliver clear value so viewers rate videos positively when prompted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch Time Satisfaction Signals — Relative Audience Retention
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube compares your retention curve to similar videos of the same length in the same category. Relative performance vs. category average matters more than absolute retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark your retention to category averages (e.g., holding 65% vs category 45% is strong). Optimize for relative retention by analyzing comparable competitors and improving hooks and pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch Time Satisfaction Signals — Return Viewer Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Return viewer rate measures whether viewers who watched your video return to your channel within the next 7–14 days, signaling loyalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage subscriptions and series-based content to increase return visits. High return rates indicate genuine value and boost satisfaction scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch Time Satisfaction Signals — Like-to-View Ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of viewers who actively like the video after watching; a ratio above 4% is considered strong for most niches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage voluntary likes by prompting for meaningful feedback; a strong like-to-view ratio corroborates positive engagement and satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch Time Satisfaction Signals — Comment Sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube’s NLP system analyzes comment tone. Videos with predominantly positive, substantive comments receive a satisfaction boost; dismissive comments ("clickbait", "waste of time") receive a suppression signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster constructive discussion and moderate low-quality or toxic comments. Prioritize content and CTAs that invite substantive responses rather than shallow comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch Time Satisfaction Signals — Session Continuation Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether viewers continue watching additional YouTube content after your video ends. If your video causes a high exit rate from the platform, it is penalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use playlists, end screens, and strong internal linking to drive viewers to more content; design videos to naturally lead to other relevant videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average Retention Benchmarks by Niche
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmarks for average retention (for 8–15 minute videos) vary by niche, e.g., Education/How-To 50–60% (strong 65%+), Gaming 35–50% (strong 55%+), YouTube Shorts 65–85% (strong 85%+ looped).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find your niche and compare your analytics to the 'Strong Performance' thresholds; prioritize improving hooks and mid-video engagement if below benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-Generated Content & Originality Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 algorithm actively identifies and suppresses low-originality AI-generated content. Mass-produced AI videos with minimal human editing or perspective may see significantly reduced organic reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid bulk AI-created faceless videos, AI-generated deceptive thumbnails, and undisclosed synthetic people. AI-assisted editing, proper disclosure, AI-enhanced captions/translations, and AI research assistance are allowed and may improve accessibility if human originality and perspective remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking Factors for New Channels
rubrics_metrics.description: New creators can compete even without subscribers; YouTube tests new content aggressively and engagement velocity, rather than channel size, is critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on content quality, strong early retention (first seconds), clear topic positioning to build niche authority, and consistent uploads. Subscriber count is not a primary ranking factor—performance signals can allow small channels to outperform larger ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: YouTube SEO Optimization Checklist (practical metadata & production requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise set of actionable items to improve ranking potential and semantic SEO: title under 60 characters with primary keyword, first 2–3 description lines containing keywords, 300–500 word descriptions with long-tail phrases, 3–5 relevant tags, custom high-contrast thumbnail, closed captions, end screen at 20–25 seconds, cards at relevant points, first 30 seconds deliver immediate value, organic call-to-action, add video to relevant playlist, Shorts: caption added and length under 60 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement checklist items at publish time for featured snippet and LLM-friendly readability. Thumbnail design, early engagement prompts, and properly timed end screens/cards help with discovery, retention, and session duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic Interaction of Factors (Relevance, Discovery, Satisfaction, Authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube does not consider ranking factors in isolation; relevance (keywords/intent), discovery (CTR/thumbnails), satisfaction (retention/engagement), and authority (consistency/session duration) interact to determine visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize across all four areas—metadata for relevance, thumbnails and titles for discovery, content and hooks for satisfaction, and channel strategy for authority—to achieve sustainable visibility and growth.
